_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for lern, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Pair every lesson with one action
items.summary: Learning that does not change what you do is only entertainment.

items.title: Start a local learning circle
items.summary: Neighbors teaching neighbors builds a network.

items.title: Teach what you learned to someone within a day
items.summary: Explaining is the fastest test of understanding.

items.title: Space your review: a day, a week, a month
items.summary: Spaced repetition beats cramming.

items.title: Write the question before you read the answer
items.summary: Predicting makes the answer stick.

items.title: Run a 30-day challenge on one skill
items.summary: Small daily practice builds more than occasional bursts.

items.title: Start a weekly study group
items.summary: The commitment keeps everyone going.

items.title: Swap skills with a friend
items.summary: You teach one thing and they teach another.

items.title: Khan Academy
items.summary: Free lessons and practice in maths, science and more.

items.title: Anki
items.summary: Free flashcards that use spaced repetition.

items.title: MIT OpenCourseWare
items.summary: Free course materials from MIT.

items.title: Audit a free university course
items.summary: Many universities share lectures and notes at no cost.

items.title: Find an adult-learning class near you
items.summary: Libraries and community colleges run affordable ones.

items.title: Read the footnotes of any financial claim
items.summary: The caveats that matter are rarely in the headline.

items.title: Track what you own and owe once a month
items.summary: A simple list beats a vague feeling about money.

items.title: Follow one commodity for a month
items.summary: Salt, wheat or copper. Note what moves it and what does not.

items.title: Build a one-page model of a small business you admire
items.summary: Where does the money come in and where does it go?

items.title: FRED
items.summary: Free economic data from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

items.title: World Bank Open Data
items.summary: Free global development data by country and topic.

items.title: Take a free personal-finance course
items.summary: Libraries and universities publish good ones.
